scope: Output quality: three complete seven-slide decks (21 slides), plus one inspected chart with explicit precision as a control. This is a bounded review, not an exhaustive quality clearance.
method: Actual MCP stdio render_deck_spec → render_deck_thumbnails at density100 → inspect PNGs → inspect embedded SVG geometry/text → submit_visual_review for all21 primary slides. Bundled LibreOfficeDev26.8.0.0.alpha0 and the existing private fontconfig.
limitations: p-style is a local ignored template; modern-yellow is the shipped reproducible equivalent.
No production fixes were made. The explicit-precision control is an authored workaround.
Input heuristic scores of98–99 were not treated as visual approval; all three primary decks received changes_requested.
The extra line chart control was inspected, but its two-slide deck was not submitted as an approved complete deliverable.
No separate defect is asserted solely from whitespace preferences or the truncated line-chart domain.

findings.title: Default chart precision collapses threshold-relevant small rates to identical labels
findings.description:
## Steps to Reproduce
Render the tracked output-quality-20261002 report's modern-yellow or p-style spec through render_deck_spec, then render_deck_thumbnails at density 100. Slide 3 is a line chart with values [0.035, 0.030, 0.025, 0.022], titled as percentages of failed payments. Its stated rollback threshold is 0.030%.

## Actual Behavior
Labels read 0.04, 0.03, 0.03, 0.02. Week 2 at the threshold and Week 3 below it become indistinguishable, and endpoint labels imply a 50% rather than 37% reduction. The distortion occurs in embedded SVG text and rendered PNGs on both templates. Input score is 98 and deterministic_ready=true; the explicit all-slide visual verdict is changes_requested.

## Expected Behavior
Default formatting preserves distinctions and decision-relevant small magnitudes, with a consistent readable scale/precision. Do not silently collapse distinct values or round nonzero values to zero merely to obey a two-decimal cap. Respect explicit authored precision.

## Root Cause and Scope
svggen/value_format.go: maxAutoDecimals=2; autoValueFormat returns %.2f even after labelsAreDistinct fails. NewValueFormatter feeds this into the label path. svggen/value_format_test.go explicitly blesses the cap with the case beyond two decimals we stop. This is a residual of closed go-slide-creator-66qb, not the separate native-pattern numeric formatter in csclk.88.

## Evidence and Control
Report: tests/quality/results/output-quality-20261002/report.json. PNGs: small-rates-default.png and small-rates-explicit-3-decimals.png in the same directory. Setting chart.data.data_labels.format to %.3f through the same MCP produces 0.035, 0.030, 0.025, 0.022 legibly. This is a verified agent workaround, not an engine fix. Production source: 24cae08241bcfebb31dd64221aadffe6a4feba12; audit HEAD 87d18357.

## Validation
Existing TestAutoValueFormat and TestBarTopHeadroom tests pass despite the visible defects. Add regression coverage for small rates and a rendered check on two templates; update the test that currently endorses collapsing distinct values.
findings.acceptance: Default [0.035,0.030,0.025,0.022] labels preserve the threshold distinction and nonzero magnitudes without contradiction with the headline; explicit precision still wins; inspect before/after rendered slides on modern-yellow and p-style.

findings.title: Negative bar labels overlap category names because the lower plot edge has no label clearance
findings.description:
## Steps to Reproduce
Render the tracked output-quality-20261002 report's modern-yellow or p-style spec via MCP. Slide 4 is chart_insight/bar_chart with categories North, West, South, East and values [9,4,0,-2]. Render and inspect the full slide at density 100.

## Actual Behavior
The negative value −2 crowds/overlaps East even though both labels are short and the chart is sparse. The same geometry fails on two templates. MCP reports diagram.text_overlap at 55% (info) and still gives deterministic_ready=true / score 98. In modern-yellow's embedded SVG, East baseline y=332.6362 with font 19.2px, and −2 baseline y=319.6724 with font 16px, at identical x=683.3782: only 12.9638px separates baselines. The rendered PNG confirms the collision.

## Expected Behavior
Negative values, category labels and the zero baseline remain clearly separated without requiring the agent to shorten a four-letter category or suppress data labels.

## Root Cause
svggen/charts.go builds the scale from yMin and withBarTopHeadroom(yMax); only positive maxima receive explicit label clearance. drawLabelledAxes places categories below plotArea.Y+plotArea.H. svggen/series.go drawValueLabel puts negative values below the bar endpoint using TextBaselineTop. A minimum exactly on the domain boundary consumes the same bottom band as the categories. Reserve measured lower clearance or position the negative annotation safely; use consistent geometry in the axes and direct-label paths.

## Evidence and Scope
Report and PNG negative-bar-label.png: tests/quality/results/output-quality-20261002/. Source verified in embedded image3.svg in both PPTX files. Related closed go-slide-creator-xv1k only added positive top headroom; go-slide-creator-s1uvj.29 concerns stacked domains, not this non-stacked label collision. Existing headroom tests pass.

## Validation
Include mixed-sign and all-negative series with minima exactly on nice tick boundaries, short and long category labels, and before/after rendered slides in both templates.
findings.acceptance: The [9,4,0,-2] chart has a clear gap between −2 and East on both templates, with no text_overlap finding; test lower-edge clearance for mixed-sign and all-negative data while preserving the zero baseline and positive-label clearance.

findings.title: Make the bundled sales-pitch example a credible, actionable presentation exemplar
findings.description:
## Problem
The shipped examples/semantic/sales_pitch.yaml compiles but its seven-slide warm-coral output is not a top-quality example for agents to imitate. The rendered market-spend chart in billions inherits Acme customer benchmark, 2025 (n=42 deployments), with no visible statement that the market figures are illustrative and no actual/forecast distinction for 2026. The partnership decision exceeds its own visual label budget, falls back to plain bullets, and repeats the pilot recommendation. The final slide says ready to start when you are without an actionable next step, accountable role or timing.

## Evidence
All seven slides were rendered and visually inspected via MCP. validate_deck_spec reports decision option 2 label 66 characters >60, INPUT.SEMANTIC_PATTERN_DEGRADED on slides[5].options. render_deck_spec gives score99/deterministic_ready=true; the all-slide visual review records changes_requested. See tests/quality/results/output-quality-20261002/report.json and sales-market-source.png, sales-decision-fallback.png, sales-closing.png.

## Root Cause and Scope
This is example authoring, not renderer fabrication: the broad default source, market values, long option text and vague closing are authored in examples/semantic/sales_pitch.yaml. internal/semantic/slides/decision.go deliberately falls back when labels exceed decisionLabelMax=60. Retain that guard; make the canonical example fit it, using concise labels plus details. The existing closed ixfrr only removed an unsupported section subtitle; the open QBR chronology bead z99un covers a different example.

## Requested Change
Clearly disclose illustrative data and distinguish market assumptions/projections from the customer benchmark. Give the alternatives concise labels with useful supporting detail so the comparison and recommendation render visually. End with a concrete pilot decision/next action, role and timing (clearly illustrative rather than invented real commitments). Inspect the full revised deck, not only its schema validity.
findings.acceptance: Rendered sales_pitch shows appropriate evidence/projection disclosure, retains its visual decision treatment without SEMANTIC_PATTERN_DEGRADED, and closes with a concrete pilot action/owner/timing; review every slide and record before/after evidence.

render_arguments.spec:
# Sales pitch — semantic authoring example.
#
# A compact semantic spec for a sales/pitch deck. It exercises a different
# archetype (sales_pitch, which prefers the warm-coral template and is not an
# "executive" archetype) and a different slide rhythm than the QBR example:
# it opens with the opportunity, sizes the market, shows traction, breaks with a
# `section` divider, and lands a partnership ask. The mix of structural / text /
# chart / kpi families is deliberately varied so the deck-rhythm rules stay
# quiet — this file is meant to validate cleanly at the default strictness.
meta:
  title: Acme Analytics — Partnership Proposal
  subtitle: Turn your operational data into decisions
  archetype: sales_pitch
  audience: VP of Operations and the buying committee
  # Deck-level default source: every data slide without its own source renders it.
  source: Acme customer benchmark, 2025 (n = 42 deployments)

slides:
  - kind: title
    title: Acme Analytics
    subtitle: Turn your operational data into decisions

  - kind: executive_summary
    title: Your teams hold the data but still wait days for decisions
    takeaway: Your teams are data-rich but decision-poor — and the gap is widening.
    points:
      - Teams rebuild the same reports weekly.
      - Decisions wait days for busy analysts.
      - Real-time rivals react twice as fast.
      - The data exists but drives no decision.

  - kind: chart_insight
    title: Real-time decisioning spend overtakes batch reporting in 2025
    insight: Spend is shifting decisively from batch reporting to live decisioning.
    chart:
      type: bar_chart
      title: Decision-analytics spend ($B)
      data:
        categories: ["2023", "2024", "2025", "2026"]
        series:
          - name: Batch reporting
            values: [12, 11, 10, 9]
          - name: Real-time decisioning
            values: [6, 10, 16, 24]
    insights:
      - Real-time decisioning overtakes batch reporting within the window.
      - Buyers are consolidating onto platforms that close the loop.
      - Early adopters report faster cycle times within a quarter.

  - kind: kpi_snapshot
    title: 60+ operations teams already decide 4.2x faster with Acme
    takeaway: Early customers are already seeing the decision gap close.
    kpis:
      - { value: "60+", label: "Operations teams live" }
      - { value: "4.2x", label: "Faster decision cycle" }
      - { value: "98%", label: "Logo retention" }
      - { value: "11wk", label: "Median time to value" }

  - kind: section
    title: The Partnership We Propose

  - kind: decision
    title: A 90-day pilot on two workflows proves the value before scaling
    recommendation: Run a 90-day pilot with your operations team, instrumenting the two workflows that cost the most analyst time today.
    options:
      - label: Stand up a 90-day pilot on the two highest-cost workflows.
        recommended: true
      - Begin with a paid discovery to map data sources before committing.
      - Defer to next budget cycle and revisit once headcount frees up.

  - kind: closing
    title: Let's Build the Pilot
    subtitle: Thank you — we're ready to start when you are.
